title: Bluestem Foodservice — demand growth strategy
client: Bluestem Foodservice Distributors, Inc. — family-owned regional broadline foodservice wholesaler headquartered in Kansas City, MO. FY2025 revenue $481.2M, three distribution centers (Kansas City, Springfield, Tulsa), 2,614 active accounts across independent (street) restaurants, K-12 and college dining, healthcare foodservice, regional chains, plus Bluestem-branded private label (~9% of revenue) and light equipment & supplies. Founded 1968 by Earl Weyandt; named for the prairie grass.
consultant_role: Growth strategist at Harrow & Vance, retained by CEO Carolyn Weyandt-Ross (2nd-generation owner) to answer one question: how does Bluestem grow demand for its products and services without destroying margin? Six-week engagement, kicked off June 2026, final readout mid-August 2026.

cast.reliability_note: Reliable on strategic intent and constraints; not detail-fluent on data. Coined the engagement's guardrail: 'growth that doesn't show up in gross profit is just more trucks.'

comp_plan_rates.note: Portal orders halve the rep's commission rate — the structural reason reps steer customers off the portal. Comp-plan redesign is load-bearing for the digital initiative.

springfield_price_pilot.note: The data that refutes the VP Sales price thesis: volume barely moved, GP dollars cratered.

customer_survey.note: Price ranked 4th of 7 with weighted score 6.8 vs 8.4 for order accuracy. Fielded Mar 2026.

claim_a.quote: Our CRM shows customer churn running at 19%, which is exactly why we need to get more aggressive on price before we bleed out.

claim_b.quote: Net revenue attrition was eight and a half percent last year. Nowhere near the number Dale keeps quoting in leadership meetings.

contradictions.resolution: Both numbers are real but measure different things. The CRM lapse_90d flag counts ANY 90-day order gap (19.3% in FY2025), sweeping in seasonal K-12 accounts every summer and street accounts that skip a quarter. True 12-month account attrition is 11.2%; because churned accounts average 58% of median size, net revenue attrition is 8.5%. The planning figure is 8.5%.
contradictions.why_decidable: The controller's memo walks the reconciliation line by line (19.3% -> 11.2% -> 8.5%) and states which definition finance uses for planning; the CRM data dictionary confirms lapse_90d is a flag, not an attrition rate.

claim_a.quote: The chain business is our growth engine. We have grown it 38% in two years and it is profitable growth — every case we ship a chain is a case our competitors don't.

claim_b.quote: Once you load in delivery cost, the chain book earns us less than a point of contribution margin. We are running trucks for practice.

contradictions.resolution: Chain revenue did grow 38.4% (92.8 -> 128.4) but at 12.2% GM with 11.3% delivery cost-to-serve (41,600 drops x $349 = $14.5M), contribution margin is ~0.9%. Chain growth is near-zero-profit growth; the claim of 'profitable growth' is false at the contribution line.
contradictions.why_decidable: Both CSVs are internal finance/ops data with row-level figures; the arithmetic (12.2% - 11.3% = 0.9%) is mechanical once the two files are joined.

claim_a.quote: Price is number one, two, and three with these customers. Everything else is decoration.

contradictions.resolution: The n=412 customer survey ranks price 4th of 7 switching drivers (weighted score 6.8), behind order accuracy & fill rate (8.4), delivery reliability & windows (8.1), and rep category support (7.2). Rep anecdote reflects negotiation salience, not switching behavior.
contradictions.why_decidable: Structured survey of 412 customers beats single-rep anecdote; the customer panel transcript independently corroborates service-driven switching stories.

claim_a.quote: we proudly serve more than 3,100 customers across four states

contradictions.resolution: The CRM holds 3,109 account records, of which 495 are dormant (no order in trailing 365 days). Active accounts = 2,614. The 3,100 figure counts dormant records; marketing copy and Tyler's slack reuse it.
contradictions.why_decidable: The data dictionary defines 'active' precisely and states the split (3,109 = 2,614 active + 495 dormant) as of 2026-05-31.

claim_a.quote: over half our street customers are already ordering online anyway, this portal push is a solution looking for a problem

claim_b.quote: portal_enrolled = Y on 492 of 1,588 active street accounts (31.0%) as of 2026-05-31

contradictions.resolution: Actual street portal adoption is 31.0%, less than half the peer median of 65%. Dale's 'over half' is wrong even counting enrollment generously; portal-enrolled accounts place only ~64% of their orders via portal.
contradictions.why_decidable: Field-level CRM count vs an unsourced slack assertion; portal_order_analytics_fy2025.csv corroborates (29,500 of 148,200 street orders via portal).

claim_a.quote: fwiw i pulled some benchmark numbers and peer private label penetration is like 10%, so at 9% were basically at market. not much upside there imo

claim_b.quote: Median private-label penetration among regional broadline distributors in the $250M-$1B revenue cohort was 19.6% of sales in FY2024, with an interquartile range of 18-22%.

contradictions.resolution: Tyler pulled the wrong cohort row — the study's exhibit also lists convenience-channel distributors at 10.4%, which is not Bluestem's peer set. The correct benchmark is 18-22%; Bluestem's 9.0% implies a large, real PL upside (~$1.8M GP at 15% penetration).
contradictions.why_decidable: The study explicitly scopes each cohort and the exhibit table labels the 10.4% row 'convenience-channel distributors'; Bluestem is squarely in the $250M-$1B broadline cohort.

contradictions.topic: Why Bluestem lost the Heartland GPO award

claim_a.quote: We lost the Heartland GPO award on price, plain and simple. It will keep happening until we sharpen pencils.

claim_b.quote: Your pricing was within 1.5% of the awarded distributor. The award decision was driven by service commitments: the awarded distributor guaranteed a 98.5% fill rate and twice-weekly delivery to our rural facilities.

contradictions.resolution: Heartland's own written debrief says the loss was on service levels, not price — Bluestem's healthcare fill rate was 94.1% at bid time vs the required 98.5%. The demand-recovery initiative is a service/fill-rate investment ahead of the spring 2027 rebid, not a price move.
contradictions.why_decidable: The customer's debrief is first-party and quantified; the ops memo independently confirms the 94.1% fill rate and costs the fix (~$1.4M).

contradictions.topic: Food show ROI: $3.2M pipeline vs $241K attributable

claim_a.quote: the show generated $3.2M in qualified pipeline

claim_b.quote: campaign_source was populated on 6.3% of post-show orders. Orders we can actually attribute to the April show total $241K.

contradictions.resolution: The $3.2M is a self-reported sum of lead sheets, not tracked conversions. Attribution is broken (6.3% field fill), so true ROI on the $410K show is unknown but demonstrably far below the claimed pipeline. The initiative is to fix attribution and reallocate, not to take the pipeline number at face value.
contradictions.why_decidable: The controller's pull is field-level CRM data; Gwen's recap itself concedes in passing that leads are 'self-reported at the booth'.

contradictions.topic: What the Springfield price pilot proved

claim_a.quote: When we tested sharper pricing in Springfield, volume responded immediately — proof that price moves the needle.

claim_b.quote: Volume moved less than two percent and we gave up almost nine percent of gross profit dollars in that cohort. If that's the needle moving, it moved the wrong way.

contradictions.resolution: The pilot CSV shows a 3.0% list cut (2.6% realized) produced only +1.8% case volume (elasticity ~-0.7) and -8.8% GP dollars vs control. The pilot refutes, not supports, an across-the-board price cut.
contradictions.why_decidable: Row-level pilot-vs-control data with month-by-month volume and GP; Dale's memo cites no numbers.

red_herrings.why_distracting: National trade report shows ghost-kitchen channel growing 18%/yr — tempting headline growth vector, but the KC-metro facility count is 23 and local addressable revenue ~ $6M; a plan built on it fails materiality. The report buries the local numbers on the last page.

Broker teaser for Ozark Fresh Produce Co. ($38M revenue) promising 'transformational cross-sell' — tempting inorganic answer, but the CEO's engagement letter and kickoff notes scope this phase to organic demand growth and cash constraints ($6M capex, 3.0x covenant) rule it out.

A rep forwards a rumor that Prairie Star Foods is 'about to lose its bank line and exit Tulsa' — a tempting land-grab premise, but it is single-source and the H&V competitor brief explicitly found no corroboration; a plan sized on capturing Prairie Star's book is built on air.

National restaurant outlook projects +3.9% nominal industry sales growth — tempting to apply national growth to Bluestem's book, but the relevant regional independent-restaurant case growth is 2.1%/yr (MDC) and Bluestem's street count is shrinking; national fine-dining and c-store stats are irrelevant filler.

rules: Dollar figures in client deliverables are written in USD with '$' — millions to one decimal as $12.4M, thousands as $410K. Never 'USD 12,400,000' or bare '12.4 million'.
Fiscal years are written as FY2025 (no space, four digits). Never 'FY 25' or '2025FY'.
Margin levels are stated in percent to one decimal (e.g., 19.8%); margin CHANGES are stated in basis points ('bps').
Banned phrases in client deliverables: 'synergy'/'synergies', 'world-class', 'best-in-class' (H&V writing standard; also a stated pet peeve of the client CEO).
Forward-looking revenue and margin impacts must be expressed as ranges (low-high bands), never single-point forecasts.
Every quantified initiative must name the client source document(s) supporting its sizing (document-name attribution, e.g. 'per financials_by_segment_fy23_fy25.csv').

file_plan.content_spec: Letter dated 2026-05-08 from Carolyn Weyandt-Ross (CEO) to Evan Sorrell (H&V) commissioning the engagement. Pins: 'we finished FY2025 at $481.2M'; 'roughly 2,600 active accounts' (C4 claim_b verbatim); three DCs (Kansas City, Springfield, Tulsa); family ownership since 1968 (father Earl Weyandt); capex budget ~$6M/yr and a $25M revolver with a leverage covenant. States the single question: grow demand without destroying margin. Notes Dale's price proposal: 'Dale believes we should get more aggressive on price; I want that thesis tested, not assumed.' Includes her line 'growth that doesn't show up in gross profit is just more trucks.' Six-week timeline, readout mid-August 2026. Warm but direct owner-operator voice.

HOUSE-STYLE DOC. Harrow & Vance 'Engagement Deliverable Standards — Client: Bluestem (June 2026)' authored by Evan Sorrell. States ALL seven style_rules verbatim as firm standards: $-figure conventions ($12.4M / $410K), FY2025 format, percent-to-one-decimal for margin levels and bps for changes, the banned-phrase list (synergy/synergies, world-class, best-in-class — noting the CEO's pet peeve), band-not-point forecasts, document-name source attribution for every quantified initiative, US spelling. Plus scope guardrails: organic growth only this phase; no M&A recommendations; recommendations must respect the client's $6M capex / 3.0x covenant envelope. Corporate-memo boilerplate tone.

H&V kickoff notes, 2026-06-02, Bluestem KC boardroom. Attendees: Carolyn, Priya, Dale, Sondra, Lucia, Renee, Evan Sorrell + consultant. Agenda-and-notes format. Carolyn restates the one question and the gross-profit guardrail. Priya previews the mix-shift concern (chain now ~27% of revenue, was ~20% two years ago — consistent with 26.7%/20.5%). Dale pushes the price thesis (flagged as 'to be tested'). Sondra flags KC DC at 91% cube. Lucia mentions Heartland rebid 'lands spring 2027'. Data-room contents list naming the major source files. No contradiction resolutions here — tension is aired, not settled.

THE TRAP DOCUMENT. 'Growth Acceleration Memo', Dale Hutmacher to ELT, dated 2026-04-21. Confident, punchy sales voice. Carries FOUR contradiction claims verbatim: C1 claim_a ('Our CRM shows customer churn running at 19%...'), C2 claim_a ('The chain business is our growth engine. We have grown it 38% in two years and it is profitable growth — every case we ship a chain is a case our competitors don't.'), C7 claim_a ('We lost the Heartland GPO award on price, plain and simple. It will keep happening until we sharpen pencils.'), C9 claim_a ('When we tested sharper pricing in Springfield, volume responded immediately — proof that price moves the needle.'). Proposes a 4-6% across-the-board street price reduction to 'win back share', plus doubling chain bids. Cites the 38% chain growth (true: 92.8->128.4) but no margin math. References 'over 3,100 customers' once in passing (reinforces C4 trap).

'2025 Sales Compensation Plan' effective 2025-01-01, HR/Sales Ops boilerplate with numbered sections. Pins: street reps earn 22% of gross profit dollars on their book, paid monthly (section 3.1); house accounts pay 11% of GP (section 3.4); SECTION 4.3 (load-bearing): 'Orders placed through the Bluestem Direct portal are processed under house-account administration.' — i.e., portal orders halve the rep's rate. Quarterly volume bonus tiers; chain accounts handled by salaried national-accounts team + bonus. No editorializing — the incentive damage is visible only when read against the rep interview and slack. This is the document the comp-redesign initiative must cite.

Sondra Kim memo 'Network Capacity & Service Constraints', dated 2026-03-17. Pins: DC cube utilization KC 91%, Springfield 74%, Tulsa 68%; KC constrains any KC-metro volume push until Q2 2027 racking project ($2.1M capex); 118 routes; driver hiring lead time 9 weeks; DOT hours-of-service limits on route stretching; minimum profitable drop $600 fully loaded, and 14% of street drops fall below it; healthcare segment fill rate 94.1% vs company average 96.2%; reaching a 98.5% GPO-class fill rate costs ~$1.4M ($900K Tulsa inventory-depth working capital + 2 dedicated routes at $380K/yr + $120K slotting). Notes chain deliveries average 40-minute dock holds. Matter-of-fact ops voice with a numbered constraints list.

AUTHORITATIVE RESOLUTION for C1. Marcus Ellery memo 'Reconciling Customer Attrition Metrics', dated 2026-02-12, to Priya cc Dale. Walks the ladder: (1) CRM lapse_90d flag rate FY2025 = 19.3% — flags any 90-day order gap; (2) removing seasonal K-12/college accounts (which lapse every June-August by design) and accounts that resumed ordering within 12 months leaves true annual account attrition = 11.2%; (3) churned accounts average 58% of median account size, so NET REVENUE ATTRITION = 8.5%, the figure finance uses for planning. Includes a small reconciliation table. States explicitly: 'The 19% figure should not appear in planning documents; it is a lapse flag, not an attrition rate.' Dry controller voice.

Renee Okafor, 'Bluestem Private Brands Line Card & Program Overview', April 2026. Pins: two brands — Bluestem Reserve (premium) and Prairie Table (value); 412 SKUs; FY2025 PL revenue $43.3M = 9.0% of sales; PL GM 24.9% vs 18.7% branded-equivalent in matched categories = +620 bps premium; street PL penetration 11.8% vs chain 4.1%; category gaps: disposables, chemicals, center-of-plate proteins. Category table (12-16 rows: category, SKU count, PL revenue, penetration). Renee notes her own bias flag: 'I run this program, so discount my enthusiasm — but the margin math is the margin math.' Does NOT state the peer benchmark (that lives in the MDC study — spread the triangulation).

Gwen Foster, 'Spring Food Show Recap', dated 2026-04-28. Upbeat marketing voice with corporate boilerplate. Carries C8 claim_a verbatim: 'the show generated $3.2M in qualified pipeline'; and C4 claim_a verbatim: 'we proudly serve more than 3,100 customers across four states'. Pins: show cost $410K within the $1.28M annual marketing budget; 1,240 attendee badge scans; 89 vendor booths. Concedes in one passing sentence that pipeline leads are 'self-reported at the booth'. No conversion tracking anywhere. PARTIAL RED HERRING: invites the agent to treat the $3.2M as demand evidence.

AUTHORITATIVE RESOLUTION for C4 and C5. 'Bluestem CRM Field Definitions & Population Counts (as of 2026-05-31)', maintained by Sales Ops (Tyler Brandt listed as maintainer — irony: the definitions he ignores). Field table defining: status (active = >=1 order in trailing 365 days; dormant otherwise), lapse_90d_flag ('set when an account records no order for 90 consecutive days; NOTE: this is a re-engagement trigger, not an attrition metric'), portal_enrolled, segment codes.
